section_summary.extract_value: This 'Statistical Analyses' section (unnamed study) describes the analytic procedures: sex-specific EFAs on the BAS-2, independent-samples and one-sample t-tests (including comparisons to Tylka & Wood-Barcalow's Study 3 community means), and bivariate correlations examining body appreciation with BMI, self-esteem, life satisfaction, age, and (for women) weight discrepancy; curvilinear relations with BMI were also considered for men. The section does not report sample size, demographic details (country, percent white, mean age, education), BMI measurement method, or numeric correlation coefficients.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: 'To examine the factor structure of the BAS-2, we computed principal-axis exploratory factor analysis (EFA) for women and men separately...'; 'An independent-samples t-test was used to compare scores between women and men in our sample. We also conducted one-sample t-tests to compare scores between our participants and the community sample means reported in Tylka and Wood-Barcalow's (2015b) Study 3...'; 'bivariate correlations were used to establish convergent validity in terms of significant associations between body appreciation, BMI, self-esteem, life satisfaction, and (for women only) weight discrepancy.'
